assumptions: The chunk-chain fields at holder + 0x13b0 and + 0x1400 advance by 8 on a chunk reset and the next chunk's data comes from the chain; the exact linking invariant of that chain is not pinned, only the observed stores and the per-chunk 0x200 free.
The record-table walk assumes the removed record is present in its bucket chain; a missing record would not terminate the walk in the binary either, so the model raises instead of looping.

The two 0x5d4a6a0 outputs are treated as built strings whose contents are the record strings' ranges; the builder's allocation behaviour is a model parameter (short form by default), not a pinned claim.

The guard pair 0x606ca40 / 0x60d52f0 is described only by its observed call order (open before each cursor read, close after each pop and each record free, close as the routine's tail jump); no lock or unlock semantics is claimed.
The source-level names and kinds of the holder, the subobject, the records, the table and the callback are not pinned; only field offsets and the transition rules are.
Arithmetic on the record count and the tail counter is wrapping subtract of 1, matching the sub forms in the excerpt.

exits.condition: record count reaches zero, in the entry check or after a record
exits.form: tail decrement of the dword at holder + 0x1444, call 0x60d57c0 with holder + 0xa10, canary check, tail jump to 0x60d52f0 with the subobject

exits.condition: canary mismatch on the tail path
exits.form: call to the stack-check failure PLT
jumps to 0x5d52e22 and 0x5d52e2c outside this routine's FDE, unpinned

close.order: after each list pop before the element is destroyed, after each record free before the callback, and as the routine's final tail jump

open.order: at entry, after each list pop (so before the next cursor read), and once after each record callback

holder_fields.record_count: holder + 0x1330, qword, decremented once per removed record
holder_fields.record_head: holder + 0x1328, head record pointer, re-read each loop iteration
holder_fields.subobject: holder + 0x700, passed to the guard pair
holder_fields.tail_argument: holder + 0xa10, passed to 0x60d57c0 on the tail path
holder_fields.tail_counter: holder + 0x1444, dword, decremented once on the tail path

list_a.rule: pop elements in order; null slots are skipped after the pop; popping the last slot of a chunk frees that chunk's 0x200 buffer and installs the next chunk from the chain; the loop ends when the cursor equals the end field

list_b.rule: same shape as list A, with the 0x5d8d820 destructor and 0x290 free size

phase_order: record removal loop while the count is nonzero

record.bucket_key: record + 0x08, divided by the table modulus for the bucket index
record.callback_arguments: holder, dword at record + 0x60, first built string, second built string, dword at record + 0x50, qword at record + 0x58

record_loop.build_calls: 0x5d4a6a0 twice per record, with (output, string begin, string begin + size) for string A then string B, call-shape only
record_loop.disposal_order: record string B, then record string A, then the record free, then the count decrement, then the guard close, then the callback, then the guard open, then built string B, then built string A
record_loop.string_rule: data pointer at string base + 0x00, capacity at string base + 0x10; short form when the pointer equals the string base + 0x10 address, else sized delete (pointer, capacity + 1)

routine.canary: fs:0x28 stored at rsp + 0x88, checked on the tail path
routine.returns: nothing; the routine ends in a tail jump to 0x60d52f0

sole_caller.rule: compares the qword at 0x64ed5d0 with zero, calls 0x606d9f0 with the same argument when nonzero, writes 2 into the TLS slot at fs:0 - 0x3f8, then tail-jumps to the routine with the argument unchanged

unlink.bucket_index: record field + 0x08 modulo the table modulus at holder + 0x1320
unlink.head_field_address_as_predecessor: a bucket slot may hold the head-field address (holder + 0x1328); storing a successor into that address advances the head
unlink.predecessor_walk: start at the bucket slot value and follow next links until a node whose next equals the record; that node, or the head-field address, is the predecessor

rules.bucket_head_case_cross_bucket_successor: store the predecessor into the successor's bucket slot; if the bucket slot held the head-field address, store the successor into the head field; clear the record's bucket slot; store the successor into the predecessor link
rules.bucket_head_case_null_successor: if the predecessor equals the head-field address, store the successor into the head field; clear the bucket slot; store the successor into the predecessor link
rules.bucket_head_case_same_bucket_successor: store the successor into the predecessor link only
rules.deeper_case: store the successor into the predecessor link, plus a predecessor store into the successor's bucket slot when the successor's bucket differs; no bucket clear and no head store
